status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026 and not yet checked by the translation workers. Informal ты throughout; a male speaker where the verb shows it.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Letters That Look Familiar, Part 1
lessons.description: Some Russian letters look like English ones and sound nothing like them: в is v, н is n, р is r, and с is s. Read вино, нос, река, and сок.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Stress Changes the Vowel, Part 1
lessons.description: An o without the stress is said as a. Hear both kinds of o in молоко, хорошо, окно, and вода.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Soft Sign, Part 1
lessons.description: The soft sign ь softens the sound before it, and can change the word. Hear брат against брать, and мат against мать.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Letter Ы, Part 1
lessons.description: The letter ы is a sound English does not have, made further back in the mouth than the i of bit. Hear it in ты, мы, сын, and рыба.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb идти, to go, changes its ending to say who is going. Spot what changes: иду, идёшь, идёт, идём.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of идти, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are off to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: Russian has no word for the or a. For more than one, the ending changes: собака becomes собаки, and дом becomes дома.

lessons.title: Patterns - Words That Match, Part 1
lessons.description: A describing word matches the thing it describes, whether a he-word, a she-word, an it-word, or many: новый, новая, новое, новые.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: A Russian yes-or-no question can keep the same words in the same order as the statement. Only the voice rises.
words: This is the bus to Moscow.
Is this the bus to Moscow?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: To say something is not so, put не in front of the verb. Nothing else in the sentence changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - No Word for Is, Part 1
lessons.description: In the present, Russian simply leaves out am, is, and are. I am a student is I student.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come First, Part 1
lessons.description: As in English, the describing word comes before the thing it describes, and matches it.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb идти, to go on foot, at work in whole sentences, and ехать, which Russian uses for going on wheels.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. Russian says I have as at me there is: у меня есть.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: No word for is, and the describing word still matches: белый, красные, высокая, маленькие.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways. The verb changes for a trip finished, a trip under way, and a trip to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
